topStories.headline: Great Highway Ballot Measure Officially Qualifies for November Vote
topStories.dek: San Francisco voters will decide for a second time whether to reopen the former Upper Great Highway to weekday car traffic, after elections officials confirmed the 'Great Highway for Everyone Act' gathered enough signatures.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's Department of Elections confirmed on July 23 that a measure to reopen the Upper Great Highway to cars has officially qualified for the November 2026 ballot. The 'Great Highway for Everyone Act,' spearheaded by the group Great Highway for Everyone, submitted more than 15,600 signatures to city officials — well above the roughly 10,600 required for ballot qualification.

If approved, the measure would reopen the two-mile stretch of the former coastal road to private vehicles on weekdays, while keeping it closed to cars on weekends and holidays, effectively reversing portions of Proposition K, which was approved by approximately 54% of San Francisco voters in November 2024. That earlier vote transformed the Upper Great Highway into Sunset Dunes Park, which has been open to pedestrians, cyclists, and skaters since March 2025.

District 4 Supervisor Alan Wong has been a public supporter of restoring weekday vehicle access. Earlier in 2026, Wong attempted to place the measure on the June ballot but was unsuccessful, after which he pledged support for the community-driven petition effort. Opponents of the new measure warn that reopening the highway to cars would require the removal of park features including picnic areas, seating, and the skate park — a process that city analysts from the SFMTA and SF Recreation and Parks estimated could cost up to $14 million.

A separate but related cost question has also emerged: according to an SFMTA analysis reported by SFist, restoring and replacing aging traffic signals along the Upper Great Highway would cost approximately $13.2 million if the road were reopened to vehicles. Supporters of the park contend that the measure, if passed, would undo a popular and heavily used public space that has drawn visitors from across the city. The measure will appear on the citywide November 3 ballot.

topStories.headline: Ocean Beach Senior Housing Permits Resubmitted — But Project Remains 'On Hiatus'
topStories.dek: Developers of the stalled 199-unit affordable senior housing complex at 1234 Great Highway resubmitted preliminary permits in mid-July, keeping the project alive while financing remains unresolved.
topStories.body:
Preliminary project permits for the proposed 199-unit affordable senior housing complex at 1234 Great Highway in the Outer Sunset were resubmitted on July 15, 2026, but the project's manager confirmed it remains officially 'on hiatus.' The Tenderloin Neighborhood Development Corporation (TNDC) and Self-Help for the Elderly, the joint developers, placed the project on an extended pause in January 2026 due to financing challenges.

The proposed development would replace the existing Motel 6 at the site — a narrow, roughly 0.8-acre lot bounded by Great Highway and La Playa Street, just across from the west end of Golden Gate Park and Ocean Beach. The eight-story building would contain 88 studios, 107 one-bedroom units, and four two-bedroom apartments, all reserved for low-income seniors, with a portion set aside for formerly homeless seniors. A single-story adult day health care center is also part of the plan.

According to Mission Local, project manager Jacob Goldstein wrote that a path forward depends significantly on California's Proposition I, a state bond measure on the November ballot that would authorize $11.25 billion in bonds for income-qualified housing. If Proposition I passes, TNDC plans to restart the financing process in January 2027, with construction potentially beginning in early 2028 and taking approximately two years to complete.

The project has faced neighborhood opposition since its inception, though housing advocates point out that the Outer Sunset contributes less than 1% of the city's new housing supply despite containing nearly 10% of San Francisco's population. The resubmission of permits signals the developers' continued commitment to eventually moving the project forward.

topStories.headline: Sunset District Home Prices Hit Multi-Year High as Bidding Wars Intensify
topStories.dek: A new market analysis shows Sunset District homes closing at more than 130% of list price in 2026, with a median of just 12 days on market — the most competitive conditions the area has seen in over a decade.
topStories.body:
A comprehensive market report published this week by Kinoko Real Estate, drawing on closed MLS data current as of July 21, 2026, reveals that the Sunset District is experiencing its most competitive home-buying environment in more than a decade. Closed sales across the Inner, Central, and Outer Sunset neighborhoods are showing 2026 sale prices running at 130% or more of list price, with homes closing in a median of just 12 days.

The Outer Sunset continues to offer the lowest entry price of the three sub-neighborhoods even as it appreciates the fastest. Inner Sunset condos and TIC units — which make up roughly 40% of that neighborhood's sales — provide a lower-cost entry point compared to the single-family home market, which dominates Central and Outer Sunset sales at approximately 94% of transactions.

The data reflects a citywide trend of strong buyer demand on San Francisco's west side. Real estate data service Redfin scored the Sunset District at 94 out of 100 on its competitiveness index, noting that most homes attract multiple offers, often with waived contingencies, and that average sale prices have been running about 32% above list price. Hot homes have been going pending in as few as nine days.

For buyers, the report notes that late fall and January historically bring somewhat reduced competition, while sellers are advised that spring remains the strongest season for maximizing both speed and price. The analysis underscores the tension between the neighborhood's high desirability and the limited affordable housing supply, which advocates say makes projects like the stalled 1234 Great Highway development all the more critical.

moreNews.headline: West Portal Has Become a Bona Fide Restaurant Destination
moreNews.body: A June 2026 profile in the SF Standard declared West Portal a full-fledged culinary hotbed, noting that the neighborhood — once considered a quiet, old-fashioned strip — has become a place people travel to on purpose to eat, even from across the city. Recent arrivals like Elena's Mexican Restaurant, Hardware Coffee Co., and the steakhouse-bar Tur have joined long-standing spots like Little Original Joe's and Trattoria da Vittorio. The corridor on West Portal Avenue has drawn comparisons to other neighborhood dining destinations, with the Standard noting it was 'like a sleeping giant surrounded by $5 million homes but stuck in 1985' before its recent dining renaissance.

moreNews.headline: Green Apple Books' Inner Sunset Location Gets Literary Co-Working Space Upstairs
moreNews.body: The long-empty mezzanine above Green Apple Books on the Park at 1231 9th Avenue in the Inner Sunset has been filled by a writer-focused co-working space called the Backstory Above, SFist reported in January 2026. The space, which maintains a library-silence policy in keeping with the bookstore below, offers monthly memberships and daily drop-in passes. Green Apple Books on the Park, a branch of the beloved San Francisco independent bookseller founded in 1967, opened its Inner Sunset location in 2014 adjacent to Golden Gate Park. The addition of a dedicated literary workspace adds a new dimension to one of the neighborhood's most beloved commercial anchors.

moreNews.headline: Shirley Chisholm Village Community Room Now Open via Children's After School Arts
moreNews.body: After more than a year of neighborhood frustration over a locked, unused community room at the 135-unit Shirley Chisholm Village affordable housing complex at 1360 43rd Avenue in the Outer Sunset, a resolution arrived in April 2026. Children's After School Arts (CASA) signed a lease for the space — now branded the 'CASA Clubhouse' — and opened it to the community in June 2026. The 749-square-foot community room is available for public reservation, while CASA also uses the broader 1,562-square-foot space for its own art and wellness programming. Developer MidPen Housing had faced community criticism for delaying the room's opening pending the identification of a nonprofit tenant.

restaurants.name: Outerlands
restaurants.description: Beloved Outer Sunset destination famous for Dutch baby pancakes and house-baked bread, with organic, height-of-season ingredients and a rustic beachy interior.

restaurants.name: San Tung
restaurants.description: Legendary Inner Sunset institution known citywide for its addictive dry-fried chicken wings, noodles, and dumplings — perennial lines out the door are part of the experience.

restaurants.name: Andytown Coffee Roasters
restaurants.description: Founded in 2014 by Michael McCrory and Lauren Crabbe, this neighborhood anchor roasts small-batch beans in-house and is celebrated for the 'Snowy Plover' espresso soda with housemade whipped cream.

restaurants.name: Devil's Teeth Baking Company
restaurants.description: Cult-favorite Outer Sunset bakery renowned for its buttermilk biscuit breakfast sandwiches, cheddar bacon beer muffins, and pastries.

restaurants.name: Trouble Coffee
restaurants.description: Quirky Outer Sunset original offering espresso, fresh whole coconuts, and thick slices of signature cinnamon-sugar toast at a driftwood-adorned parklet.

restaurants.name: Hook Fish Co.
restaurants.description: Beloved Outer Sunset fish shack serving ultra-fresh fish tacos, fish burritos, and plates with a standout house hot sauce bar.

restaurants.name: Fiorella
restaurants.description: Popular Inner Sunset trattoria known for fresh pizza and pasta, with a sought-after rooftop seating area.

restaurants.name: Art's Café
restaurants.type: Classic American diner with Korean influences
restaurants.description: Long-running Inner Sunset diner serving big-portioned, affordable breakfasts and lunches — named best breakfast in the city more than once over its 30-plus years in business.

restaurants.name: Marnee Thai
restaurants.description: Inner Sunset staple for authentic Thai cuisine, particularly praised for its khao soy chicken and Thai-style fried rice.

restaurants.name: The Riptide
restaurants.description: 84-year-old beachside honky-tonk on Taraval with a brick floor, fireplace decorated with sand dollars, karaoke nights, and live music.

restaurants.name: White Cap
restaurants.description: Stylish cocktail bar on outer Taraval Street serving the Sunset's best Manhattans, martinis, and boozy slushies in a cozy upscale setting.

restaurants.name: The Little Shamrock
restaurants.description: One of San Francisco's oldest pubs, a cash-only neighborhood institution on the Inner Sunset's southern edge with dark wood, mismatched furniture, and an authentic Irish pub atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Java Beach Café
restaurants.description: Casual Outer Sunset café near Ocean Beach serving coffees, breakfast burritos, lavash wraps, and specialty bagels — a popular pre-beach stop.

restaurants.name: Arizmendi Bakery
restaurants.description: Worker-owned cooperative bakery beloved for freshly baked pastries and breads, with a public parklet outside for neighbors to gather.

restaurants.name: Judahlicious
restaurants.description: Outer Sunset vegan spot serving heaping açaí bowls, fresh juices, and plant-based dishes popular with surfers and health-conscious locals alike.

restaurants.name: Toyose
restaurants.description: A hole-in-the-wall Korean restaurant in a converted Noriega Street garage, open until midnight or later, serving soju-paired comfort classics.

restaurants.name: Dumpling Kitchen
restaurants.description: Highly regarded Taraval Street dumpling house serving Shanghai-style pan-fried pork buns, soup dumplings, and hand-rolled noodles.

restaurants.name: Caché
restaurants.description: Elegant French café on 9th Avenue in the Inner Sunset, opened in 2025 by two chefs with Michelin-starred French restaurant experience, known for its sea bream sashimi and lobster rolls.

restaurants.name: Tur
restaurants.description: West Portal's splashy newcomer offering prime steaks, craft cocktails including the signature Butcher's Old Fashioned, in a cozy dim-lit dining room.

restaurants.name: Little Original Joe's
restaurants.description: West Portal institution serving classic Italian-American comfort food including pasta, chops, and the neighborhood's favorite chicken dishes.

restaurants.name: Elena's Mexican Restaurant
restaurants.description: One of San Francisco's Best New Restaurants of 2024 according to The Infatuation, this West Portal Mexican spot earned rave reviews for its vibrant atmosphere and authentic dishes.

restaurants.name: Trattoria da Vittorio
restaurants.description: Beloved West Portal Italian spot fitting seamlessly into the neighborhood's small-town charm, with classic pastas and a welcoming dining room.

restaurants.name: Hardware Coffee Co.
restaurants.description: Stylish West Portal café from the Bacchus restaurant group (Spruce, Village Pub), offering exceptional espresso drinks and pastries in a beautifully designed space.

restaurants.name: Polly Ann Ice Cream
restaurants.description: Outer Sunset neighborhood ice cream shop famous for its extensive rotating roster of flavors and the novelty spinning flavor wheel for the adventurous.

restaurants.name: Snowbird Coffee
restaurants.description: Cozy Inner Sunset multi-roaster café recommended by SF.gov as the perfect neighborhood morning coffee stop, with something for every palate.

hotels.name: Sunset Edwardian Bed and Breakfast at Golden Gate Park
hotels.description: Charming Edwardian-style B&B in the Inner Sunset offering complimentary breakfast and an ideal base for exploring Golden Gate Park and the N-Judah corridor.

shops.name: Green Apple Books on the Park
shops.description: Inner Sunset branch of San Francisco's beloved Green Apple Books, situated one block from Golden Gate Park, stocking new books, magazines, and novelties; now home to the Backstory Above literary co-working space upstairs.

shops.name: Black Bird Bookstore & Café
shops.description: Light-filled, minimalist Outer Sunset bookstore with an attached café serving seasonal drinks including Rocky's matcha, with regular author events.

shops.name: Mollusk Surf Shop
shops.description: The definitive Outer Sunset surf shop, carrying wetsuits, surfboards, casual summer wear, and sunglasses — a gathering place for the neighborhood's surf community.

shops.name: General Store
shops.description: Curated Judah Street shop beloved for well-made sweaters, jewelry, household items, and small treasures, with a photogenic backyard garden.

shops.name: San Franpsycho
shops.description: Iconic Sunset District shop offering locally designed and screen-printed clothes, accessories, and art celebrating San Francisco surf and skate culture.

shops.name: Pemulis Water and Power
shops.description: Eclectic Outer Sunset shop selling surf gear, curated vintage goods, and hand-poured candles made on site in the back of the store.

shops.name: Sunset Shapers
shops.description: Fully integrated Outer Sunset surfboard manufacturing center open since 2010, building boards start-to-finish with in-house shaping, art, and glassing.

shops.name: Hunt & Gather
shops.description: Inner Sunset gallery-style shop featuring locally made and thoughtfully curated art, home goods, and gifts.

shops.name: The Kira Shop
shops.description: Charming Outer Sunset shop stocking whimsical gifts, home goods, and accessories with a beachy neighborhood sensibility.

shops.name: Amazing Fantasy Comics & Games
shops.description: Inner Sunset comic book shop with over 1,000 graphic novels and new issues arriving every Wednesday, a favorite stop on the 9th Avenue corridor.

shops.name: Unwined
shops.description: West Portal neighborhood wine shop popular as an after-work stop, offering a well-curated selection of bottles and knowledgeable staff.

artEntertainment.name: Stern Grove
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's treasured eucalyptus-lined natural amphitheater, home to the nation's longest-running free outdoor music festival since 1938, hosting major artists every Sunday in summer.

artEntertainment.name: Conservatory of Flowers
artEntertainment.description: Golden Gate Park's magnificent Victorian-era glass conservatory housing rare tropical plants, special exhibitions, and — as of July 2026 — a blooming corpse flower.
artEntertainment.address: 100 John F. Kennedy Dr, Golden Gate Park

artEntertainment.name: de Young Museum
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's premier fine arts museum in Golden Gate Park, featuring American art, international textiles, and a free observation tower with panoramic city views.
artEntertainment.address: 50 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, Golden Gate Park

artEntertainment.name: California Academy of Sciences
artEntertainment.type: Natural history museum, planetarium, and aquarium
artEntertainment.description: World-class science institution in Golden Gate Park housing a living rainforest, coral reef aquarium, Morrison Planetarium, and a renowned living roof.
artEntertainment.address: 55 Music Concourse Dr, Golden Gate Park

artEntertainment.name: Sunset Dunes Park
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's newest park, created from the former Upper Great Highway, stretching two miles along Ocean Beach with a skate park, picnic areas, murals, and coastal trail from Golden Gate Park to the SF Zoo.
artEntertainment.address: Great Highway between Lincoln Way & Sloat Blvd

artEntertainment.name: SF Women Artists Gallery
artEntertainment.description: Inner Sunset gallery operated by and showcasing works from San Francisco women artists, with rotating exhibitions and community programming.

artEntertainment.name: Ocean Beach
artEntertainment.type: Public beach and coastal recreation area
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's wild 3.5-mile Pacific coastline offering kite flying, surfing, bonfires in designated fire rings, and dramatic sunsets — the defining natural feature of the Sunset District.

artEntertainment.name: Forest Hill Clubhouse
artEntertainment.description: Landmark 1919 Craftsman-style community clubhouse designed by renowned architect Bernard Maybeck, serving the historic Forest Hill residence park neighborhood.

gymsRecreation.name: Yoga Beach
gymsRecreation.description: Bright, welcoming Outer Sunset yoga studio with natural light and ocean breezes, offering all-levels classes just blocks from the beach at 4501 Irving Street.

gymsRecreation.name: Ocean Beach Yoga SF
gymsRecreation.description: Outer Sunset yoga studio providing a personalized approach to yoga, offering new students a complimentary second class.

gymsRecreation.name: Studio By Live Better
gymsRecreation.description: Intimate Outer Sunset mind-body studio offering yoga, Pilates, and wellness classes in a clean, calm space a short walk from the beach.

gymsRecreation.name: Sunset Gym
gymsRecreation.description: Local fitness gym in the Inner Sunset serving the neighborhood with comprehensive equipment and studio spaces.

gymsRecreation.name: Stern Grove
gymsRecreation.description: Beloved 33-acre park featuring the natural eucalyptus and redwood-lined amphitheater, lawns, picnic areas, and tennis courts at the southern edge of the Sunset.

gymsRecreation.name: Sunset Dunes Skate Park
gymsRecreation.description: Free public skate park within the new Sunset Dunes coastal park on the former Great Highway, open to skateboarders and inline skaters of all skill levels.

gymsRecreation.name: Koret Health and Recreation Center (UCSF)
gymsRecreation.description: Full-service fitness and recreation facility on the UCSF Parnassus campus at the Inner Sunset's eastern edge, open to UCSF affiliates and community members.

gymsRecreation.name: San Francisco Zoo
gymsRecreation.description: Established in the 1920s at the southern end of the Outer Sunset, the SF Zoo houses over 2,000 animals and connects directly to Ocean Beach and Sunset Dunes Park.

gymsRecreation.name: Golden Gate Park
gymsRecreation.description: San Francisco's iconic 1,017-acre urban park bordering the Inner and Outer Sunset to the north, offering trails, sports fields, fly-casting pools, bike paths, and world-class museums.
gymsRecreation.address: Bordered by Fulton St, Stanyan St, Lincoln Way & the Pacific Ocean

gymsRecreation.type: Surf shop with surf culture community hub
gymsRecreation.description: Beyond retail, Mollusk's Judah Street location is the heart of the Outer Sunset surf community, connecting residents with local surf instructors, wetsuit rentals, and board repairs.
